description: We are a team of College Students from the University of Central Missouri. We are interested in participating in the Abandoned but not Forgotten track!
summary:
In 2018, a dust storm darkened Mars and the Opportunity rover went silent. It was built to last 90 days. It worked for almost 15 years. It is still there.
With Still Here, we wanted students to meet it. Our project addresses the “Abandoned but not Forgotten” challenge with a VR story for ages 12 to 18, built on NASA terrain data and 3D models. From the start menu, students choose one of three missions: Opportunity, InSight or the Ingenuity helicopter.
Opportunity’s story begins at the end. A student stands beside the silent rover on its real final site. Then the story flashes back. The student assembles the rover in a NASA clean room, launches it on a Delta II rocket, lands it, and follows it to the rocks where it found hematite, evidence of ancient water. Back in the present, the rover is no longer a stranger.
Each part a student fits explains its purpose, and the final choice asks what the evidence supports. This makes distant hardware personal, and shows how engineering leads to discovery.
Still Here is designed for classrooms, libraries and museums, and built to grow: more Mars missions, then the machines left on the Moon.
details:
Our project, Still Here, is an educational VR experience that lets students explore the stories of spacecraft left on Mars, with Opportunity as our main experience.

How it plays:

Each mission follows the same arc for the Opportunity rover, the Insight Lander, and the Ingenuity helicopter: present, flashback, present.

  • Arrive: meet the silent machine at its final site and point at its parts to learn what each one did.
  • Flashback: assemble its components, experience its launch, and land on Mars.
  • Explore: with Opportunity, investigate rocks through three guided activities: hematite “blueberries”, a jarosite mineral reading, and deciding what the findings suggest about past water. With Ingenuity, fly its first flight after Perseverance sets it down. With Insight, record data on Marsquakes.
  • Legacy: return to the present and try to wake it up. It never answers, just like the real missions.

How we built it:

  • Unity and C#, with OpenXR and the XR Interaction Toolkit for movement, grabbing, and interactive controls, for Meta Quest 2.
  • The ground is NASA’s HiRISE elevation model of the exact spot where Opportunity stopped, at 1 m resolution. MOLA data extends it to the horizon, including Endeavour Crater.
  • NASA 3D models of Opportunity, InSight, Ingenuity and Perseverance.
  • ElevenLabs voice narration for the story, instructions and scientific explanations. The recordings are stored in the project, so narration plays without an internet connection.
  • Claude Code, Codex, and Canva AI were our main SI/AI tools
  • Unity’s XR Device Simulator for development and testing without a headset.

What makes it creative:

What makes our project creative is the combination of storytelling and participation. Players meet a silent machine, discover how it reached Mars, and take part in activities inspired by its scientific work. The final return to its legacy connects those discoveries to the people and engineering behind the mission.

Impact and what we considered:

Our intended impact is to make space exploration more engaging for students aged 12–18 and encourage curiosity about science and engineering. We considered scientific accuracy, readable instructions, audio guidance, VR comfort, and our hackathon timeline. We also clearly distinguish educational simplifications from real instrument operation—and evidence of past water from proof of life.
